question: Do two independently planned search routes together retain gains lost when either route commits to a single method? Both finalists are outputs of the ordinary SuperAgent. The narrower and wider catalogue get their own full search and can choose any available single or blend.
procedure: Replay ten pairs of previously finished original-catalogue and expanded-catalogue solutions covering five training-held folds in each of two budget regimes. Both solutions must be cold-reload verified, on the identical task packets. Combine each solution's own confirmed members on the exact same three internal holdouts using trusted row and class order. Apply the already implemented leave-one-fold-out weight rule from study_task1_inference_reuse.fit_weight to these two whole solutions. If two foldwise gains and >=.003 pooled support a specific share use the median, else use an equal blend. Compare to both original endpoints, including cases where all three give the same prediction. Seal all ten before the new grading pass.
resources: No new base model training for the replay. Report actual sum of the two historical training costs per row of the experiment without claiming that two searches are a same-cost single policy. The two complete CV collections reuse course training data.
gate: To qualify for a fresh autonomous equal-total-budget experiment, the 48-cap replay must improve at least .003 pooled against each original endpoint, each 32-cap pooled comparison must be nonnegative, and the largest loss against either endpoint in any fold may not exceed .005. No external task labels, course designated validation, official test or API.
